questions.question: Three vectors [latex] \vec{p}, \vec{q} [/latex] and [latex] \vec{r} [/latex] are given as [latex] \vec{p}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k} [/latex] [latex] \overrightarrow{\mathrm{q}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}} [/latex] [latex] \vec{r}=2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k} [/latex] Which of the following is/are CORRECT?

(A) [latex] \vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r})=(\vec{p} \cdot \vec{r}) \vec{q}-(\vec{p} \cdot \vec{q}) \vec{r} [/latex]
(This is always true for any three given vectors)

(B) We know that [latex] \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} [/latex] is always true but [latex] \vec{a} \times \vec{b} \neq \vec{b} \times \vec{a} [/latex] because [latex] \vec{a} \times \vec{b}=-\vec{b} \times \vec{a} [/latex]
This can be true only when [latex] \vec{a} \times \vec{b}=0 [/latex]
So, [latex] \quad \vec{r} \cdot(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})=\vec{r} .(\vec{q} \times \vec{p}) [/latex]
[latex] \vec{r} \cdot(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})=-\vec{r} \cdot(\vec{p} \times \vec{q}) [/latex]
This can be true if
[latex] \begin{aligned} \vec{r} \cdot(\vec{p} \times q) & =0 \\ \vec{p} \times \vec{q} & =\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+j \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex] (\vec{r} \cdot \vec{p} \times \vec{q})=0 [/latex] this is true in this case

[latex] \vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r}) \perp \vec{p} [/latex] and [latex] (\vec{p} \times \vec{q}) \times \vec{r}) \perp \vec{r} [/latex]
So, [latex] (\vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r}) \neq(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})) \times \vec{r} [/latex]

(D) [latex] \vec{p} \times(\vec{q} \times \vec{r})+\vec{q} \times(\vec{r} \times \vec{p})+\vec{r} \times(\vec{p} \times \vec{q})=\overrightarrow{0} [/latex]
[latex] (\vec{p} . \vec{r}) \vec{q}-(\vec{p} . \vec{q}) \vec{r}+(\vec{q} . \vec{p}) \vec{p}-(\vec{q} \cdot \vec{r}) \vec{p}+(\vec{r} . \vec{q}) \vec{p}-(\vec{r} . \vec{q})) \vec{q} [/latex]
[latex] 0=0 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} & \vec{p} \cdot \vec{r}=\vec{r} \cdot \vec{p} \\ & \vec{p} \cdot \vec{q}=\vec{q} \cdot \vec{p} \\ & \vec{q} \cdot \vec{r}=\vec{r} \cdot \vec{q} \end{aligned} [/latex]
(Hence proved)

questions.question: A circular settling tank is to be designed for primary treatment of sewage of a flow rate of 10 million liters/day. Assume a detention period of 2.0 hours and surface loading rate of 40000 liters [latex] / \mathrm{m}^{2} / [/latex] day. questions.explanation_html:
Given,
Discharge, [latex] \mathrm{Q}=10 \mathrm{MLD} [/latex]
Detention period, [latex] \mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{d}}=2 \mathrm{hr} [/latex]
Over flow rate, [latex] \mathrm{V}_{0}=40,000 [/latex] litres [latex] / \mathrm{m}^{2} / [/latex] day
[latex] \mathrm{H}= [/latex] ?

As, Surface area of tank [latex] =\frac{\text { Discharge }}{\text { Over flow rate }}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{V}_{0}} [/latex]
So,
[latex] \begin{aligned} & \text { S.A. }=\frac{10 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~L} / \text { day }}{40,000 \mathrm{~L} / \mathrm{m}^{2} / \text { day }} \\ & \text { S.A }=250 \mathrm{~m}^{2} \end{aligned} [/latex]
Volume of tank [latex] (V)=Q \times t_{d} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} & =\frac{10 \times 10^{6} \times 10^{-3}}{24} \times 2 \mathrm{~m}^{3} \\ & \mathrm{~V}=833.33 \mathrm{~m}^{3} \end{aligned} [/latex]
Hence,
Height of water in tank or Height of setting zone
[latex] \begin{aligned} H & =\frac{833.33 \mathrm{~m}^{3}}{250 \mathrm{~m}^{2}} \\ H & =3.33 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned} [/latex]
Note: In reality, height of water in tank OR height of settling zone is estimated by above approach but if the bottom of sedimentation tank is assumed to be sloping or hoppered (i.e sludge zone is also considered) then height of water in tank is determined as follows:
Using,
Volume of tank [latex] (V)=D^{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4} H+0.011 D\right) [/latex]
As,

[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { S.A. } & =\frac{\pi}{4} D^{2}=250 \mathrm{~m}^{2} \\ D & =17.835 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned} [/latex]

So, [latex] 833.33=(17.835)^{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4} H+0.011(17.835)\right) [/latex]
So, [latex] \mathrm{H}=3.085 \mathrm{~m} [/latex]

questions.question: A vertical summit curve on a freight corridor is formed at the intersection of two gradients, [latex] +3.0 \% [/latex] and [latex] -5.0 \% [/latex]. Assume the following: Only large-sized trucks are allowed on this corridor. Design speed [latex] =80 \mathrm{kmph} [/latex] Eye height of truck drivers above the road surface [latex] =2.30 \mathrm{~m} [/latex] Height of object above the road surface for which trucks need to stop [latex] =0.35 \mathrm{~m} [/latex] Total reaction time of the truck drivers [latex] =2.0 \mathrm{~s} [/latex] Coefficient of longitudinal friction of the road [latex] =0.36 [/latex] Stopping sight distance gets compesnated on the gradient. The design length of the summit curve (in meters) to accommodate the stopping sight distance is _____ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.topic: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
questions.explanation_html:
Step 1: Algebraic difference of gradients
[latex] A = |+3 - (-5)| = 8% = 0.08 [/latex]

Step 2: Conversion of speed
[latex] V = \frac{80 \times 1000}{3600} = 22.22 , \text{m/s} [/latex]

Step 3: Reaction distance
[latex] S_r = V \times t = 22.22 \times 2 = 44.44 , \text{m} [/latex]

Step 4: Braking distance
[latex] S_b = \frac{V^2}{2 g f} = \frac{(22.22)^2}{2 \times 9.81 \times 0.36} = 69.94 , \text{m} [/latex]

Step 5: Stopping Sight Distance (SSD)
[latex] S = S_r + S_b = 44.44 + 69.94 = 114.38 , \text{m} [/latex]

Step 6: Length of summit curve (SSD criterion)
For summit curve, when
[latex] L \ge S [/latex]

[latex] L = \frac{A S^2}{2(\sqrt{h_1} + \sqrt{h_2})^2} [/latex]

[latex] \sqrt{h_1} = \sqrt{2.30} = 1.517, \quad \sqrt{h_2} = \sqrt{0.35} = 0.592 [/latex]

[latex] (\sqrt{h_1} + \sqrt{h_2})^2 = (2.109)^2 = 4.448 [/latex]

[latex] L = \frac{0.08 \times (114.38)^2}{2 \times 4.448} = \frac{1046.6}{8.896} = 117.70 , \text{m} [/latex]

Check condition:
[latex] L = 117.70 , \text{m} \ge S = 114.38 , \text{m} [/latex]
Hence, the condition is satisfied.
